title: Detect Data Drift in Production
summary: Implement the two workhorse drift statistics, Population Stability Index and the two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov distance, then build a per-feature drift report that tells you which inputs moved.

NaNInSoftmax.hint: A NaN or inf in PSI comes from log(0) or dividing by an empty bin. Clip both proportions to at least eps before taking the log.

hints.test_psi_matches_definition: Edges are [-inf, *unique(quantile(reference, interior probabilities)), +inf]. Count with np.histogram, divide by n, clip to eps, then sum (c − r)·ln(c / r).
hints.test_psi_identical_distributions_is_zero: Identical inputs give identical bin proportions, so every (c − r) term is 0.
hints.test_psi_detects_shift: A mean shift of one standard deviation moves a lot of mass between quantile bins, so PSI rises well above 0.25.
hints.test_psi_constant_reference_is_finite: Duplicate quantiles collapse under np.unique. With the outer ±inf edges there are still at least two bins, and eps clipping keeps the log finite.
hints.test_ks_known_values: D = max over all observed x of |F_a(x) − F_b(x)|. Identical samples give 0, and samples that don't overlap give 1.
hints.test_ks_matches_brute_force: Sort each sample. np.searchsorted(sorted, x, side='right') / n is the empirical CDF at x. Evaluate it at every value in both samples.
hints.test_psi_level: Common rule of thumb: below 0.1 is 'none', 0.1 up to 0.25 is 'moderate', and 0.25 or more is 'major'.
hints.test_drift_report_flags_shifted_features: Compute PSI and KS per feature from the reference dict. A feature is drifted when psi >= psi_threshold. List drifted names alphabetically.
hints.test_drift_report_missing_feature: If a reference feature is missing from current, that's a broken data contract. Raise ValueError.
hints.test_inputs_not_mutated: Copy arrays with np.asarray(..., dtype=float) before sorting. Never sort the caller's data in place.
